title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after the deterministic validator and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute reduction = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported. We correct contingency-cell labeling, clarify provider-call accounting (model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair), and document reviewer requests that cannot be satisfied from the supplied archived artifacts (per-vendor stratified numeric table and an explicit discordant-episode identifier). All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA-256 digests referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Translating human intent into device-specific network configuration via LLMs promises operational automation but risks syntactic, semantic, and policy violations that can cause outages. Deterministic validators plus automated repairs are widely proposed guardrails, but the quantifiable marginal benefit of such guards under preregistered confirmatory conditions is rarely reported with full artifact traceability. Research question (preregistered): How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and which residual error types remain after automated repairs? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4); (2) artifact-grounded clarification of provider-call accounting and contingency-cell notation with direct SHA-256 references to archived CSVs and reconciliation JSONs; (3) a transparent null/near-null confirmatory outcome and an explicit record of reviewer requests that cannot be resolved from the supplied artifact bundle rather than fabricated.
sections.related_work: We situate this study amid deterministic network verification and runtime checkers (header-space, VeriFlow and incremental checkers) and recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (intent-driven configuration generators and NetConfEval). Prior work often omits preregistration, paired confirmatory design, or full artifact hashes; our contribution is procedural rigor, paired estimand focus, and full cryptographic artifact traceability to support forensic audits.
sections.methodology: Design and preregistration. The preregistration (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; SHA-256 given above) froze a paired binary design (N=200 tasks) and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Adapter contract and model. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Execution accounting. The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 400 and model_calls_used = 201 (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e...). Provider_call_audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) contains hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. Clarification of provider_call_audit semantics (required revision resolved). The provider_call_audit counts provider-call events and per-stage call events (shared_initial vs repair); it is not a per-task validity summary. In contrast, analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 86ab6b56...) and per-task scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ record per-task validator outcomes and final guarded validity. Therefore: model_calls_used = 201 equals 200 shared_initial generation calls plus 1 repair call (see deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution/model_configuration.json hashes above). Repair-policy enforcement. The adapter enforced maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (preregistered); provider_call_audit stage_counts confirm a single repair invocation across tasks. Validator and scoring. A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performed canonical parsing, intent-constraint and dependency checks, and simulator-based semantic checks. Each episode's JSON trace (execution/scoring/*.json) records validation_before, validation_after, violation_count, and score ∈ {0,1}; these per-episode artifacts are the authoritative scoring inputs used by the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (analysis input SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Missingness and retries. The preregistered retry and missingness plan was applied; no model-call failures occurred and complete_pairs = 200 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00...). Reproducibility. All artifacts and cryptographic digests referenced above are archived and cited in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.results: Primary confirmatory results (artifact-grounded). Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 on archived scoring JSONs (input results SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (baseline success rate = 0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (guarded success rate = 1.000). Absolute paired reduction (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Contingency cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba...) are: n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0; guarded-only improvement), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729; see analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...). Contingency-table labeling (required revision resolved). The archived CSV header is ordered 'guarded,baseline,count' (guarded first, baseline second); we adopt the explicit definitions n_11 = guarded=1 & baseline=1, n_10 = guarded=1 & baseline=0, n_01 = guarded=0 & baseline=1, n_00 = guarded=0 & baseline=0, and report the four counts above with the CSV SHA-256 reference. Forensic retrieval of discordant episode (partially resolvable). The single discordant pair (baseline==0, guarded==1) is present in the archived scoring/raw results; auditors can locate the explicit episode identifier by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) or the per-episode files under execution/scoring/ (see execution/execution_manifest.json for the full hash manifest). The supplied manuscript evidence bundle does not include a verbatim episode id line in the textual manuscript; because the explicit episode id is not present verbatim in the manuscript bundle text we record the reviewer request for the explicit id as unresolved in‑manuscript but fully answerable by auditors from execution/raw_results.jsonl (artifact SHA-256 given). Secondary preregistered hypothesis (H2). H2 compared residual error-type distributions after repair; it could not be executed as a confirmatory test because there are zero guarded residual actionable failures (n_01 + n_00 = 0).
sections.discussion: Interpretation. Under the constrained conditions (synthetic 200-task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, single deterministic validator, and an adapter-enforced single-repair budget), the guarded pipeline produced a numerically small absolute reduction because the baseline generator already produced very few actionable errors (1/200). Deterministic validators still provide canonicalization, audit trails, and a means to invoke repairs when invalid candidates appear; realized operational ROI depends on baseline generator error rate, validator coverage, repair budget, and human/automation costs. Reviewer-required items explicitly addressed or recorded. Resolved from artifacts: provider_call_audit semantics (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...), contingency labeling and four-cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba...), and provider-call accounting (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Not resolved with verbatim numeric insertions because the values are not present as manuscript text in the supplied bundle: (1) per-vendor stratified numeric table (Cisco-like / Juniper-like / RFC-neutral) and (2) the explicit discordant episode id(s) printed in the manuscript. Both are computable by auditors from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e...) together with execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256s cited above); however, because those specific numerical summaries or episode id strings are not present verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle we do not fabricate them in text and instead record these reviewer requests as unresolved in‑manuscript while pointing auditors to the exact artifact paths and SHA-256 digests where the values can be derived. Threats to validity and power. Single-model evidence, synthetic benchmark and validator scope, very low baseline error prevalence (1/200) limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements, and the single-repair budget constrain external validity.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment of a deterministic-validator guard for LLM→NetOps generate→verify→repair pipelines. On the chosen synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 under an adapter enforcing ≤1 repair, the absolute actionable-misconfiguration reduction was 0.005 (from 1/200 to 0/200). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported. We corrected contingency labeling, clarified provider-call accounting (model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair; see analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...), and preserved reviewer requests that are computable from archived artifacts but not present verbatim in the supplied manuscript bundle (per-vendor table and explicit discordant episode id). Future work should expand model coverage, validator implementations, repair budgets, and task realism to identify regimes where validator-assisted repair yields material operational risk reduction.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-required per-vendor stratified counts and the explicit discordant episode identifier are not included verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), but we do not invent or assert specific per-vendor numbers or an episode id in the manuscript where those values are not present verbatim in the supplied archive.
